Hi Marissa — thanks for the summary and for the call. Confirming a few items from Acme's side: 

1) Procurement path: For pilots <$50k we typically allow credit card payments; anything over ~$50k goes through our PO process and requires finance approval. For strategic vendor relationships we prefer direct PO so we can manage contracts centrally.

2) Marketplace: We like the convenience of AWS Marketplace for smaller purchases, but for enterprise contracts (SLA/custom terms) our procurement team prefers direct PO and a signed SOW. If you can be listed on AWS Marketplace that's a plus and speeds pilot procurement.

3) Budget owners / signatories: 
   - Finance sponsor / budget owner: Priya Shah (Finance Business Partner) — cc'd.
   - Economic buyer: Tom Rivera, Director of Product (will review ROI and sign-off).
   - Legal / signatory: VP Legal (Laura Bennett) will sign final MSAs.

I've attached our internal PO process doc to this reply which outlines routing and typical SLA expectations. Also looping in Priya to schedule the procurement/finance sync.

Attachments: Acme_PO_Process.pdf

Got it — I'll put together a short MAP with two tracks and a suggested timeline. A couple quick notes from product/ops: 
- Marketplace track: fastest for pilot — no MSA negotiation, immediate procurement via card or marketplace listing. Good for evaluating run-rate and token usage.
- Direct PO track: allow 2–3 weeks for finance/contract routing for a small pilot; legal sign-off (Laura) is usually the gating item for custom terms.
- Fallback: suggest offering a card-based pilot for 30 days (minimal friction) while parallelizing PO paperwork for production-stage rollout.

Aditya — once you share the two pricing paths I can drop them into the MAP and include recommended cadence for ramp and billing cadence.

Vivek
